# Evidence Requirements Checklist: Provider Conformance, Compatibility and Composition

**Purpose**: Standard-depth requirements-quality review of input attribution, fail-closed reporting, bounded ownership and local/CI evidence before implementation.
**Created**: 2026-10-22
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)
**Audience / timing**: Maintainers and qualification-evidence reviewers during draft PR review, before implementation authorization.

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and the maintainer's request for an assisted assessment.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is reviewer-owned. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means requirements-quality approval, not implementation completion. Generation and the assessment below do not set approval markers.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are all attribution inputs specified, including inventory, source bytes, locks, package/runtime identities, configuration, capabilities and actual environment? [Completeness, Spec FR-018, SC-008]
- [ ] CHK002 Are observed parameterized runtime witnesses and exact case/binding/matrix identities required rather than self-reported labels, aggregate counts or exit codes? [Completeness, Spec FR-002, FR-018, FR-020]
- [ ] CHK003 Are final statuses, authorized exclusions, append-only attempts and independent aggregate evaluation defined for every expected case? [Completeness, Spec FR-020]
- [ ] CHK004 Are isolation, ownership, cleanup/recovery guidance and protection of concurrent runs and user resources explicitly required? [Completeness, Spec FR-016, FR-024]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 Are source/input stability and conditional lower-level evidence reuse defined so historical or mismatched passes cannot qualify changed inputs? [Clarity, Spec FR-018]
- [ ] CHK006 Is report verification distinguished from fresh runtime execution, focused diagnosis and full five-profile qualification? [Clarity, Spec FR-020..021, FR-024]
- [ ] CHK007 Are finite operation, contention, child, profile and cleanup observation budgets quantified without widening inherited deadlines or implying actual settlement? [Clarity, Spec FR-009, FR-016, SC-007]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK008 Are local and CI requirements based on identical catalogs and acceptance rules while preserving each profile's actual assigned packages and environment? [Consistency, Spec FR-018, FR-021]
- [ ] CHK009 Are retry and expected-negative rules consistent, so genuine failures remain disqualifying while deliberate red/green children prove the intended assertion? [Consistency, Spec FR-019..020]
- [ ] CHK010 Are sanitation requirements consistent for public output, private retained diagnostics and legacy imports, with synthetic fault stores explicitly separate from evidence? [Consistency, Spec FR-022, SC-007]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK011 Are missing, duplicate, unknown, stale, altered, mandatory-skipped and interrupted result challenges mapped to measurable rejection criteria and an unaltered passing control? [Measurability, Spec FR-020, SC-006]
- [ ] CHK012 Are witness origin, proof-byte correspondence and actual package resolution required beyond matching filenames, hashes or optimistic report booleans? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec FR-012, FR-018, SC-008]
- [ ] CHK013 Are safe diagnostic identities, classification and corrective guidance specified without permitting raw exception, connection, payload or path disclosure? [Measurability, Spec FR-022, SC-007]

## Scenario and Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK014 Are cancellation, runner loss, non-success jobs, absent reports and failed uploads/downloads explicitly disqualifying even after partial successful work? [Coverage, Spec FR-017, FR-020..021, US5 scenarios 2,3]
- [ ] CHK015 Are live children, failed exit observation, overlapping runs, hostile/symlinked roots and retained ownership addressed without broad deletion, forced release or name-based termination? [Edge Cases, Spec FR-009, FR-016, US4 scenario 3]
- [ ] CHK016 Are malformed/oversized evidence, duplicate schema keys, path escapes, output flooding and unknown diagnostics covered by bounded, explicit failure requirements rather than truncation into success? [Edge Cases, Spec FR-016, FR-020, FR-022]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK017 Are transient capture, retained diagnostics, report/proof collections, concurrency and scratch-space limits concrete, with inadequate resources yielding incomplete qualification? [Boundedness, Spec FR-016..017, SC-007]
- [ ] CHK018 Are CI permissions, action pinning, artifact allowlists/retention and forbidden publishing/cloud/governance changes documented without presenting planned workflow behavior as delivered? [Completeness, Spec FR-021..024, Assumptions]

## Dependencies, Assumptions and Conflicts

- [ ] CHK019 Are local no-secret/no-service prerequisites, future service-profile absence and runner-capacity verification explicit without silent simulation or reduced coverage? [Dependency, Spec FR-017, SC-004]
- [ ] CHK020 Are the report's trust boundary and finite scope stated clearly enough to exclude hostile-provider attestation, untested cross-products and blanket support or deployment authority? [Clarity, Spec FR-014, FR-023..024, Assumptions]

## Assisted Assessment

The maintainer requested assessment as well as generation. All 20 criteria have
supporting written requirements; no unresolved requirements-quality blocker or
product decision was identified. This is an advisory assessment, not reviewer
approval, runtime evidence or implementation authorization. All markers remain
unchecked for the reviewer.

| CHK004,007,015,017 | [Harness: Finite Work and Isolation](../contracts/harness.md); [data model: Validation and Bounds / Ownership](../data-model.md); [quickstart: Failure and Owned Recovery](../quickstart.md); [acceptance QC-33..36](../contracts/acceptance.md) |
| CHK010,013,016 | [Evidence: Diagnostics and Public Projection / Deterministic Evaluation](../contracts/evidence.md); [harness: output capture bounds and overflow](../contracts/harness.md); [acceptance QC-34,44,48](../contracts/acceptance.md) |
| CHK014,018..019 | [Evidence: CI Profiles and Aggregate Check](../contracts/evidence.md); [plan: Technical Context](../plan.md); [quickstart: Prerequisites and Safe Workspace](../quickstart.md); [acceptance QC-37,45..46](../contracts/acceptance.md) |
| CHK020 | [Evidence: trust boundary / Scope Labels](../contracts/evidence.md); [matrix: Unsupported Choices and Reporting](../contracts/matrix.md); [spec: Assumptions](../spec.md) |

Implementation watch-outs, not missing requirements: measure the planned CI
runner's capacity for at least 24 GiB private scratch and the mandatory real
large-transfer workload; inadequate capacity blocks qualification. Sanitizing
only uploads is insufficient: retained diagnostics must be safe before
persistence, raw output must stay transient and bounded, and output overflow
must fail rather than hide witnesses. The five profiles and six predecessor
acceptance gates remain actual future execution obligations.
